basic_info: 40-year-old female presenting with anxiety around the time of period and concerns about breast lumps
present_illness: Onset of anxiety symptoms around the time of her period, with associated concerns about breast lumps. The lumps are present in both breasts, with the left one being denser. They have been present for a while, since she had her son, and have not changed much except for possibly getting slightly smaller. They are tender, especially in the left breast, and she recalls experiencing similar soreness during breastfeeding. The lumps are small, movable, and have not changed significantly in size or appearance over time. Anxiety symptoms spike the week before her period and then occur randomly afterward. The patient has not noticed any changes in the size, tenderness, or consistency of the lumps related to her menstrual cycle. The anxiety symptoms were particularly severe in November and December, with spikes the week before her period and random occurrences afterward, though they have improved recently. The patient also experienced irritability in the past, especially when on progesterone, which was not directly linked to her periods.
past_history: No prior breast imaging or biopsy reported. Pap smear in 2019, unrelated to breasts. No prior thyroid function tests or sex hormone level evaluations reported. No history of progesterone use reported.
physical_exam: Breast examination reveals small, movable lumps in both breasts, with the left one being denser and more tender. No nipple discharge or skin changes observed.
aux_exam: No prior breast imaging reported. Patient is willing to undergo evaluation if needed. No prior thyroid function tests or sex hormone level evaluations reported.
